- [x] Have you followed the guidelines in our [Contributing](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) document?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pulls) for the same change?
- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your changes? [Here's an example](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/Library/Homebrew/test/PATH_spec.rb).
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew style` with your changes locally?
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew tests` with your changes locally?

-----

Migrate some of the audit rules to RuboCop (closes #7392).

Each rule is implemented in its own commit which might make reviewing easier.

## Migrated Rules
- separate `make` calls
- `env :std` has been deprecated in homebrew/core
- `env :userpaths` has been deprecated
- don't use `"#{foo + "bar"}"`
- require `openjdk` or `:java` dependency to use `JAVA_HOME`
- use `bin` instead of `prefix + "bin"`
- use `pkgshare` instead of `share/"foo"`
- use `:optional` or `:recommended ` instead of `build.with?` or `build.without?` in dependencies (not in homebrew/core)
- style now warns when using deprecated `build.include?`
- don't need `require "formula"`

issue_context.title: Migrate audit rules to rubocops
issue_context.body:
In https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/7371/files I have added lots of `# TODO: check could be in RuboCop` comments to `Library/Homebrew/dev-cmd/audit.rb`. These indicate that the audit check/problem below does not rely on `Formula` state so could be moved to a RuboCop (https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/tree/master/Library/Homebrew/rubocops) to be faster, more reliable and provided in-editor to users.

No need to say "I'm planning on working on this" or similar in this issue but feel free to open a PR that doesn't work (yet!) and ask for help.
comments: @Rylan12 one for you if you hadn't seen this 😉

> @Rylan12 one for you if you hadn't seen this 😉

Hmm looks like my contributions have been following a little bit of a pattern... 🤔 

Thanks for pointing it out!

#7909 Takes care of all but two of these.

Here are the remaining ones:

- `system "foo", "#{bar}"` should become `system "foo", bar`: RuboCop currently warns saying ``Prefer `to_s` over string interpolation.`` Is this sufficient? If not, should this rubocop check be removed for formulae so users don't get two style messages for the same problem?
- ~`require "formula"` is unnecessary: I can't figure out how to check for lines outside of the formula's class with rubocop so I'm not sure exactly how to do this.~ Edit: figured this one out

> * `system "foo", "#{bar}"` should become `system "foo", bar`: RuboCop currently warns saying `` Prefer `to_s` over string interpolation. `` Is this sufficient? If not, should this rubocop check be removed for formulae so users don't get two style messages for the same problem?

Yeah, I think just remove this one 👍.

review_comments: Could this do a direct method match?
This is finding strings that start with any of the keywords, not methods
Not sure I understand this but; isn't it just done by `find_instance_method_call`? What is the extra match doing?

`find_instance_method_call` gets all occurrences of `build.with?`. This includes any instances within the `install` block. The match then filters out only the instances that are part of a `depends_on` line, as that's what the cop is checking.

I wanted to have a non-regex way to do this but got stuck. One option that I thought would work would be to use `def_node_search` or `def_node_match` but I couldn't figure out how to use them properly (and didn't find much online).

Now that I'm looking at it it's possible I could, instead of using a regex, check that `n.parent`'s type is `if` and that it's parent's method name is `depends_on`. I'll look into it later today.

> I wanted to have a non-regex way to do this but got stuck.

Good enough for me. Could you add a `# TODO` for future refactoring if you decide to merge as-is?
Could this do a direct method match?

Possibly. I guess what I would need to do is find a call to `prefix` and then see if it is followed by a string that starts with any of the options.

Again, this might be a use case for `def_node_match` or `def_node_search`. If you have a resource that could explain these better that might be helpful. I looked at the instances in [`rubocops/extend/formula.rb`](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/Library/Homebrew/rubocops/extend/formula.rb#L248-L262) and on the RuboCop documentation page but it just hasn't clicked for me.

> I guess what I would need to do is find a call to `prefix` and then see if it is followed by a string that starts with any of the options.

Aye 👍.

Good enough for me to leave as-is if desired, though. Could you add a `# TODO` for future refactoring if you decide to merge as-is?
